result.description:
The Company

At Comunet, we love great tech—but what really drives us is what it makes possible. For 30 years, we’ve been helping organisations get more from their IT, whether that means tightening security, modernising legacy environments, reducing complexity, or setting them up for what’s next. We work with smart people, solve real problems, and build technology that genuinely makes life easier for our clients.? 

We’re big on curiosity, initiative, and people who genuinely enjoy figuring things out. We like teammates who can dive into a technical challenge, collaborate well, share what they know, and still keep things light along the way. Culture matters here, and we invest in it—with a strong Employee Value Proposition, Friday drinks, team events, whole-of-business catchups, and a fully stocked pantry. We work hard, support each other, and make sure there’s room to grow, experiment, and enjoy the ride.? 

We invest in our people through certified and flexible training, flexible work options, and strong support structures. We also believe in promoting from within and take pride in seeing our people grow and succeed. 



About the Role

The Support Engineer role at Comunet is not an entry-level position—it’s for someone who already has solid runs on the board and enjoys getting stuck into complex technical problems. You’ll be a key escalation point within our support team, taking ownership of issues across networking, cloud, security, infrastructure, and more. We’re looking for someone who can work with confidence, think critically, and bring the kind of hands-on experience that helps solve the tougher challenges when they land. 

At its core, this role is about keeping client and internal environments secure, stable, and performing at a high standard—but it also comes with real responsibility. This is a role for someone who can operate with a fair degree of autonomy, make sound technical decisions, and contribute meaningfully across both BAU support and project work. You’ll also help guide graduate and entry-level team members, share your knowledge, and lift the capability of the wider team through experience, mentorship, and technical leadership. 

We operate 6am - 6pm Monday to Friday to service our clients and shifts will fall within these hours on a rotating basis. 

 Applicants must have the legal right to work in Australia on an ongoing basis. 



Key Responsibilities:

Deliver high-quality IT support to our clients, with a strong focus on responsiveness, professionalism, and customer service. 

Provide guidance and mentoring to IT Support Analysts, interns, and other junior team members, helping build technical capability across the team. 

Manage support tickets effectively, ensuring client requests are accurately logged, updated, prioritised, and progressed through to resolution. 

Deliver remote and phone-based support for escalated and technology-specific issues across a broad range of client environments. 

Contribute to onsite support activities and assist with project delivery, technical implementations, and other assigned tasks as required. 

Maintain, patch, monitor, and upgrade IT environments to support reliability, performance, and security outcomes. 

Ensure work is tracked in timesheets for client services and personal development activities. 

Support and administer core IT infrastructure and cloud-based systems, applying strong technical skills across modern business environments. 



 Key technical skills:

Knowledge of basic networking (routing and switching). 

2+ years of experience in Windows Server Administration. This is expected to include familiarity with Active Directory, Group Policy, and management of common server roles. 

2+ years of experience in Microsoft 365 administration (with exposure to hybrid Exchange environments considered highly desirable). 

AWS and/or Azure skills highly desirable. 

Demonstrate a strong knowledge of security practises and controls. 



Attributes we look for:

You’ll bring at least two years of IT experience, along with relevant qualifications or certifications, and be ready to build on your existing knowledge. You’ll enjoy working with clients to solve technical challenges and help deliver stable, secure, and reliable platforms for their business. 



How to Apply

We'd love a cover letter with your CV addressing why you should be the suitable candidate to join us. 

As this is active ongoing recruitment process the position may be filled with the right applicant before the published closing date - so we encourage applications as early as possible.  

By submitting an application to Comunet, you acknowledge that we will undertake workforce screening activities including, but not limited to: Reference checks, National Crime and Right to Work Checks, Identity and certification verification.

Only candidates that are short listed will be contacted.

REDEEM SKILLS RECRUITMENT SOLUTIONS (RECRUITER) on behalf of CareSquad Pty Ltd T/A Care Squad

Role: Care Supervisor  
Employer : Caresquad Pty Ltd trading as Care Squad
Location: 214 Hampstead Rd, Clearview SA 5085 
Position: Full-time
Salary Range: $75,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation

ABOUT US

At Care Squad, we have a mission to improve the quality of life for people living with a disability, build confidence, dignity, and assistance to develop personal skills. As a small provider based in South Australia, we have a dedicated and caring team that focuses on the individual and their own personal wants, needs, and goals. 

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a compassionate and experienced Care Supervisor to lead our direct care team across aged care and disability support services. This is a full-time, ongoing supervisory role shall be responsible for overseeing the planning, coordination and delivery of high-quality, person-centred care services to older people and individuals with complex support needs and to supervise, guide and support a team of aged care workers, disability support workers and personal care workers, while ensuring all services are delivered in compliance with legislative, ethical and quality standards.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Service Coordination & Delivery

•	Coordinate, monitor and review individualised care and support services for older people and NDIS participants, ensuring services are responsive to changing client needs and aligned with their goals
•	Facilitate the development, implementation and ongoing review of individual service plans in collaboration with clients, families and multidisciplinary teams
•	Coordinate client-directed services, supporting consumer choice and control in all aspects of service delivery
•	Deliver and oversee care services using a palliative approach, providing dignified end-of-life care in accordance with best practice standards

Supervision & Workforce Leadership

•	Supervise aged care workers, disability support workers and personal care workers on a day-to-day basis, providing clear direction, mentoring and performance guidance
•	Conduct regular team briefings, support debriefs and individual supervision sessions to maintain workforce wellbeing and service quality
•	Identify training and development needs within the team and provide or coordinate relevant training, coaching and support
•	Promote independence and community participation among staff and clients alike

Risk Management & Complex Needs

•	Identify, assess and implement targeted interventions for older people at risk, including those experiencing social isolation, functional decline or complex health presentations
•	Escalate concerns appropriately and contribute to risk management planning in line with organisational policy and legislative obligations

Compliance & Governance

•	Manage legal and ethical compliance across all service activities, including adherence to the Aged Care Quality Standards, NDIS Practice Standards and relevant South Australian legislation
•	Maintain accurate client records, incident reports and service documentation in accordance with privacy and confidentiality obligations
•	Ensure all staff operate within their scope of practice and comply with relevant certifications and compliance requirements (Police Check, NDIS Worker Screening, etc.)

Partnerships & Networks

•	Develop and maintain professional networks and collaborative partnerships with health services, community organisations, allied health professionals and government agencies
•	Manage and review partnership agreements with contracted service providers, ensuring obligations are met and service quality is upheld
•	Represent Care Squad in stakeholder meetings, case conferences and community forums as required

TO BE SUCCESSFUL IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL REQUIRE:

•	AQF Certificate IV in Individual support or higher relevant qualification is required.
•	12 months full-time or equivalent part-time or casual basis employment with proven experience is required in relevant field. 
•	Demonstrated experience supervising or leading a team in a care setting is highly desirable
•	Valid Australian driver’s license is must, along with comprehensive car insurance. 
•	Applicants must be willing to accept shift allocations at client locations across metropolitan, regional, and outer regional South Australia, depending on operational requirements and client care needs. Flexibility to travel between client locations is an essential requirement of this position.
•	Strong interpersonal skills, a compassionate, patient approach.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of team.
•	A valid National Police Check, Working with Children Check and other NDIS entry level certificates are required.
•	First Aid, Manual Handling and CPR Certificate is required.
•	Sound understanding of the aged care and/or NDIS legislative frameworks

BENEFITS

•	Work in a supportive and inclusive team environment.
•	Opportunities for career development.
•	Meaningful work where you make a real impact.

About Us

JBS Australia is the largest and most respected meat and food producer in Australia. We have a strong portfolio of leading and renowned beef, lamb, pork, salmon and value-added branded products, such as AMH, Swift, Primo, Murray Valley and Huon.

JBS Australia’s Northern Division operates five strategically placed processing facilities as well as five feedlots across Queensland and New South Wales, with access to an extensive network of quality cattle. Our network provides the ability to meet the specific demands of various market segments with an extensive range of grain-fed and pasture-fed products. With approximately 15,000 employees spread across our offices, processing plants and feedlots, JBS Australia exports to more than 50 countries around the world.

About the Role

An exciting opportunity is opening for a maintenance planner for our Dinmore Site, it is a full-time role and responsible for our Dinmore site Maintenance related tasks. The annual salary for this role is not less than $79,423.00 plus superannuation.

The maintenance planer is responsible for a wide range of engineering and maintenance activities associated with the operations of multiple cattle feedlots. The maintenance planner develops and implements long-term and short-term maintenance plans for all mechanical and electrical equipment to optimize feedlot safety, quality, equipment availability, and reliability outcomes. The role provides direction and guidance to the feedlot maintenance team members to ensure the safe and efficient maintenance and repair of the electrical and mechanical assets. Additionally, the role identifies and implements continuous improvement opportunities in processes, systems, and equipment, and manages nominated capital projects.

Reporting to the plant engineer, this is a leadership position within the maintenance team. The position is hands-on, requires extensive maintenance and equipment knowledge, provides equipment solutions using sound maintenance principles, and requires the ability to lead and develop maintenance crew team members.

 Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

· Facilitate maintenance to ensure production requirements are met.

· Ensure all requested and scheduled tasks are investigated, planned, executed, completed, and closed out on time and on budget.

· Prepare and order necessary spare parts and materials for planned tasks.

· Monitor spare parts holdings and the condition of critical spares.

· Develop and maintain the sap pm equipment register (functional locations).

· Monitor maintenance employee timesheets and follow up on any comments and recommendations.

· Plan, schedule, and monitor completion of maintenance work orders.

· Program and ensure all statutory requirements are met.

· Plan, schedule, and coordinate all major repair tasks in conjunction with the feedlot engineer.

· Ensure all documentation and schematics are securely retained, updated, and maintained as required.
